title: Advanced MCP — Multiple Servers & Tool Chaining

sections.content:
## What You'll Learn

Lesson 6-9 introduced MCP and set up a single Jira server. This lesson goes deeper: multiple servers running simultaneously, chaining their tools in a single prompt, and working with the most valuable MCP servers for professional and government use.

You'll learn:
- How to run multiple MCP servers at the same time
- The GitHub MCP server — Copilot querying its own source platform
- Azure DevOps MCP — for teams on Microsoft's toolchain (common in government)
- Database MCP servers — Copilot with live read access to your data
- Slack and communication tool MCP servers
- How to chain multiple tools in one agent prompt
- Enterprise MCP controls — what your organization can restrict

## The GitHub MCP Server

The GitHub MCP server is Anthropic/GitHub's official server for accessing GitHub.com from within Copilot Agent Mode. It's distinct from the `@github` chat participant — it provides tool calls that Copilot can execute autonomously.

**Setup:**
```json
"github": {
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"],
  "env": {
    "GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN": "${env:GITHUB_TOKEN}"
  }
}
```

Create a GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) at github.com/settings/tokens with scopes: `repo`, `read:org`, `read:user`.

**Available tools:**
- `search_repositories` — search GitHub repos
- `get_file_contents` — read any file in any public (or authorized private) repo
- `list_issues` / `get_issue` — list and read issues
- `create_issue` / `update_issue` — create and update issues
- `list_pull_requests` / `get_pull_request` — PR management
- `create_pull_request` — create PRs from code changes
- `list_commits` — browse commit history
- `push_files` — push file changes to a branch

**What you can do with it:**
```
Search GitHub for the most popular Python libraries for parsing government data formats 
(specifically: CSV, XML from legacy systems, EDIFACT). List the top 5 with their GitHub 
star counts and last update dates.
```

```
I just finished implementing [feature]. Create a PR on GitHub from my current branch to main.
PR title: [feature name], description: [summarize what was built].
```

**Security:** The GitHub MCP server includes push protection — it blocks secrets from being included in any AI-generated responses and prevents secret exposure through any tool actions.

You can discover and install MCP servers from GitHub's MCP Registry directly from VS Code — open the Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P`) and search for **MCP: Browse Registry**.

## Azure DevOps MCP — The Government Standard

Many government agencies use Azure DevOps (ADO) instead of GitHub for project management. There's an MCP server for it.

**Setup:**
```json
"azure-devops": {
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["-y", "@microsoft/mcp-azure-devops"],
  "env": {
    "ADO_ORG_URL": "https://dev.azure.com/your-org",
    "ADO_PAT": "${env:ADO_TOKEN}"
  }
}
```

Create an ADO Personal Access Token at dev.azure.com/your-org/_usersSettings/tokens with Read permissions on Work Items, Code, and Build.

**Available tools:**
- `get_work_item` / `search_work_items` — read tickets
- `create_work_item` / `update_work_item` — manage work items
- `list_pull_requests` / `create_pull_request` — PR management
- `run_pipeline` — trigger CI/CD pipelines
- `get_build_status` — check build results

**Government workflow example:**
```
Search my Azure DevOps project for all User Story work items in Sprint 12 
that are currently In Progress. For each one, check if there's a corresponding 
branch in the repository. Report any stories without active branches.
```

```
I just merged PR #47 which addresses ADO work item #234. 
Update work item #234 status to Done and add a comment linking to the merge commit.
```

## Database MCP Servers — Read-Access to Live Data

Database MCP servers give Copilot read access to real databases, enabling data analysis, schema exploration, and query generation from natural language.

**PostgreSQL:**
```json
"postgres": {
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres", "${env:DATABASE_URL}"]
}
```

**SQLite:**
```json
"sqlite": {
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-sqlite", "/path/to/database.db"]
}
```

**What Copilot can do with database access:**
```
Describe the schema of the database. List all tables, their columns and types, 
and any foreign key relationships you can infer.
```

```
How many records in the transactions table were created this month? 
Break them down by status field.
```

```
I need to find all users who haven't logged in for more than 90 days 
and whose account is still marked active. Write and explain the SQL query for this.
```

**Critical security rule:** Use read-only database connections for MCP servers. Most database MCP servers support read-only mode. Never give Copilot Agent Mode write access to a production database. Configure your connection string to a read-only user:
```bash
# Read-only PostgreSQL user
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://readonly_user:pass@host/db?options=-c+default_transaction_read_only%3Don"
```

## Chaining Multiple MCP Tools in One Prompt

The real power of having multiple MCP servers is chaining them — one prompt that uses tools from several servers in sequence.

### Example 1: Bug Report to Fix to PR

With GitHub + Jira MCP running:
```
Check GitHub issues for our repository. Find any issue labeled 'bug' and 'high-priority' 
that has no linked PR. Pick the oldest one. Read the issue details fully. Find the related 
code in my workspace. Implement a fix. Create a PR with a description linking to the 
original issue. Update the Jira ticket corresponding to this GitHub issue to In Progress 
with a comment pointing to the new PR.
```

Copilot uses: `github.list_issues` → `github.get_issue` → workspace search → file edits → `github.create_pull_request` → `atlassian.update_issue`.

### Example 2: Database Anomaly to Ticket

With PostgreSQL + Azure DevOps MCP:
```
Query the audit log table for any operations performed outside business hours 
(before 7am or after 7pm) in the last 7 days. If you find any, create an Azure DevOps 
bug work item titled 'After-hours data access detected - [date range]' with the full 
query results as the description. Set priority to 1 (Critical).
```

Copilot uses: `postgres.query` → `azure-devops.create_work_item`.

### Example 3: Sprint Report

With Azure DevOps + GitHub MCP:
```
Generate a sprint summary for Sprint 15:
1. List all completed work items from ADO Sprint 15
2. For each item, find the corresponding GitHub PR (search by work item number in PR titles)
3. Get the PR merge date and reviewer count
4. Output a markdown table: Work Item | Title | PR # | Merged Date | Reviewers
```

**Enterprise MCP Controls.** If your organization uses GitHub Copilot Business or Enterprise, your GitHub organization administrator can control which MCP servers you're allowed to connect. They may set an allowlist of approved MCP servers — if your server isn't on the allowlist, Copilot will refuse to use it even if it's configured in your mcp.json.

For government users: before connecting any MCP server that accesses organizational data (databases, project management tools, file systems), check with your IT/security team whether the server is approved. The organization allowlist is the enforcement mechanism — but policy approval comes first.

sections.title: Multi-Server Setup: GitHub + Jira
sections.content:
Set up two MCP servers simultaneously and run a cross-tool workflow.

**Prerequisites:**
- Jira MCP from lesson 6-9 (already set up)
- A GitHub Personal Access Token (from github.com/settings/tokens, scopes: `repo`, `read:org`)

**Step 1 — Add GitHub MCP to your .vscode/mcp.json:**
```json
{
  "servers": {
    "atlassian": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@atlassian/mcp-atlassian"],
      "env": {
        "JIRA_URL": "https://YOUR-DOMAIN.atlassian.net",
        "JIRA_USERNAME": "your@email.com",
        "JIRA_API_TOKEN": "your-jira-token"
      }
    },
    "github": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"],
      "env": {
        "GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN": "your-github-token"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Step 2 — Reload VS Code.** Check the Tools panel — you should see tools from both servers.

**Step 3 — Cross-tool chain prompt:**
```
Search my Jira project for the highest-priority open bug ticket. Read its full details.
Then search our GitHub repository for any related open issues or PRs that might already 
address this bug. Report back: what's the bug, and is there any existing GitHub work 
addressing it or do I need to create a new issue?
```

**Step 4 — Create the GitHub issue if needed:**
```
Create a GitHub issue for this bug. Title it based on the Jira ticket title. 
In the description, include: problem summary, steps to reproduce from the Jira ticket, 
and link back to the Jira ticket ID.
```

**Verify:** Check both Jira and GitHub to confirm the information is accurate and the link is correct.

sections.title: Workshop A — Database Schema Explorer
sections.content:
Connect a database MCP server and use Copilot to understand and query it.

**For this workshop, use a SQLite database.** If you don't have one, create a sample:
```bash
npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-sqlite create-sample sample.db
```
Or use any SQLite file you have (many applications store data in SQLite: browsers, messaging apps, various tools).

**Add to .vscode/mcp.json:**
```json
"sqlite": {
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-sqlite", "./sample.db"]
}
```

**Exploration prompts (in Copilot Agent Mode):**

```
Describe the schema of this database. List every table, its columns with types, 
and any relationships between tables.
```

```
How many records are in each table? Show me a count for all tables.
```

```
What are the 5 most recently modified records across all tables? 
(Use any timestamp column you find.)
```

```
Write a SQL query that would generate a summary report of [most interesting table] 
grouped by [a category column]. Explain what the query does before running it.
```

**Key learning:** Notice that Copilot can explore a database schema and write accurate queries without you describing the schema first — it reads it directly via MCP. This is the difference between generating code that *might* work and generating code that *knows* your actual database structure.

sections.title: Workshop B — The Full Tool Chain
sections.content:
Build a complete automated workflow that spans database → analysis → project management ticket.

**Setup needed:** Database MCP (SQLite or PostgreSQL) + Jira or Azure DevOps MCP.

**The workflow: Automated anomaly detection and ticketing.**

**Step 1 — Query for anomalies:**
```
Query the database for records that look anomalous. Look for:
- Records created at unusual times (if there's a timestamp column)
- Records with null values in important columns
- Records where numerical values are far outside the normal range
List the top 5 most suspicious records with their IDs and the specific anomaly.
```

**Step 2 — Create a ticket for each finding:**
```
For each anomaly you found, create a Jira bug ticket with:
- Title: 'Data Anomaly: [brief description of the specific issue]'
- Description: the specific record details, what makes it anomalous, and suggested investigation steps
- Priority: Medium
- Label: data-quality
```

**Step 3 — Verify in Jira/ADO.** Open your project management tool and confirm the tickets were created with accurate information.

**What this demonstrates:** A realistic data monitoring workflow that generates actionable work items automatically — the kind of thing that would normally require a custom script plus manual ticket creation.

sections.title: Workshop C — MCP Security Configuration
sections.content:
Configure MCP for a security-conscious government environment.

**The problem:** You want to use MCP to connect Copilot to your work tools, but you need to:
1. Keep credentials out of version control
2. Only allow read operations on the database
3. Restrict which users can connect certain MCP servers
4. Document the approved server list for your team

**Step 1 — Create a .env file (not committed to git):**
```bash
# .env (add this file to .gitignore)
JIRA_TOKEN=your-token-here
GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_your-token
ADO_TOKEN=your-ado-pat
DB_READONLY_URL=postgresql://reader:pass@host/db
```

**Step 2 — Create mcp.json using env references:**
```json
{
  "servers": {
    "atlassian": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@atlassian/mcp-atlassian"],
      "env": {
        "JIRA_URL": "https://your-domain.atlassian.net",
        "JIRA_USERNAME": "your@email.com",
        "JIRA_API_TOKEN": "${env:JIRA_TOKEN}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Step 3 — Add .env to .gitignore:**
```bash
echo ".env" >> .gitignore
echo ".vscode/mcp.json" >> .gitignore
```

**Step 4 — Create `mcp.template.json`** (this one IS committed):
A copy of your mcp.json with placeholder values like `"YOUR_JIRA_TOKEN_HERE"` instead of `${env:}` references. This shows teammates the structure without exposing credentials.

**Step 5 — Write `MCP-SETUP.md`** documenting:
- Which MCP servers your team uses and why
- Which ones have been approved by your IT/security team
- How to create the .env file
- Any servers that are not approved (list specifically)

**Outcome:** An MCP setup that's both functional and safe to work with in a regulated environment.

sections.question: You configure a PostgreSQL MCP server with full read/write credentials. A teammate runs Copilot Agent Mode with the prompt 'Clean up the test data from the users table'. What is the risk?
options: No risk — Copilot Agent Mode won't delete data without explicit confirmation
Copilot could execute DELETE or UPDATE queries on the production database if it misidentifies which records are 'test data'
The risk is low because Copilot always previews SQL before executing
No risk — the MCP server only allows SELECT queries
sections.explanation: If you give the MCP server write credentials, Copilot Agent Mode can execute INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations on the database. With an ambiguous prompt like 'clean up test data', Copilot might delete records it incorrectly identifies as test data. Always use read-only database credentials for MCP servers. If write access is ever needed, use a dedicated staging database, verify the SQL Copilot plans to run before confirming, and never give Agent Mode write access to a production database.

sections.question: Your .vscode/mcp.json uses ${env:JIRA_TOKEN} to reference an environment variable. You commit mcp.json to GitHub. Is this safe?
options: No — GitHub will scan and find the token in the file
Yes — the ${env:JIRA_TOKEN} syntax is a reference to an environment variable, not the actual token value. The token itself is in your environment, not in the file.
Only if the repository is private
No — you must never commit any mcp.json file to version control
sections.explanation: The ${env:JIRA_TOKEN} syntax is a reference, not the actual value. The committed file contains only the placeholder text '${env:JIRA_TOKEN}' — the actual token lives in your shell environment (set via .bashrc, .env file loaded separately, or system environment variables). Anyone cloning the repository gets the mcp.json structure but not your credentials. They need to set their own environment variables with their own tokens. This is the correct pattern for sharing MCP configuration with a team.

sections.content: **Lesson 6-17 complete.** You can now run multiple MCP servers simultaneously, chain their tools across databases, project management, and code platforms in single prompts, and configure everything securely without exposing credentials. The multi-server approach transforms Copilot from a coding assistant into an integration layer across your whole technology stack. Lesson 6-18 covers Copilot for Testing — using AI to build better test suites, not just generate passing tests.
